page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 57 at top right. Above a rule: a block of italic verse (four lines) at full width. Below the rule: a heading in capitals across the full width, then a paragraph of roman text, then a block of italic verse in lines running to the foot, with a signature mark "H" at lower right. A narrow strip at the left edge of the lines is damage, not text.

l.i: Creditur, efque pia sancta propago domus,
anctorum certe tanto felicior est sors,
Quanto est illorum mors properata magis,
uanam igitur tandem iusta ratione fleatur,
Quam cito nata solo, tam cito iuncta polo?
TE caelo mutante solum, Gesnere, volucres
Te caelo mutante solum, Gesnere, feroces
Te feri gemunt colubri, sibilis lugubribus,

page.notes: The first line of the first verse block and the lines near the left edge are partly damaged; readings marked [?] are uncertain. The "H" at lower right is a signature mark and is recorded in the bottom margin as printed. Greek in the heading is transcribed as best read.
